newsitem.title: USA: Wal-Mart sees rising international sales.
newsitem.headline: Wal-Mart sees rising international sales.

text.p: Wal-Mart Stores Inc's senior manager of international operations said Friday that forecasts of $400 million in international sales for the fiscal year ending January 31, 1998, were "not unreasonable."
Les Copeland said at the retailer's annual meeting here that the increased sales would put Wal-Mart on track to boost international revenues by 32 percent this year.
Wal-Mart in the first quarter generated $6 million in profits from sales in Canada and Mexico, compared to a loss of $16 million in the same period last year, he said.
The retailer, which generates just under five percent of its total sales from international operations, said it plans to add up to 35 stores outside the U.S. as part of a continuing global expansion.
"We are ready for major global expansion," said John Menzer, Wal-Mart chief financial officer.
The expansion will include doubling the number of Supercenters stores in Brazil and Argentina, where the company also plans to open traditional Wal-Mart stores in smaller markets, he said.

Wal-Mart executives declined to identify other countries where the company it plans to expand. The retailer posted $104 billion in total sales last year and has a goal of topping $200 billion in the years ahead.

Next week it will expand its virtual shopping options, doubling to 800,000 the number of items from its Wal-Mart and Sam's Club inventories available on line. On-line shopping accounts for less than one percent of total sales for the company, Wal-Mart officials said.

At the annual meeting, shareholders overwhelmingly voted down a proposal to require Wal-Mart to monitor working conditions and ensure adequate wages were paid to vendors' workers producing goods for the retailer.
